382YE Summer Solstice winds of fortune.d: The roundup covered many matters. The Navarr weighed hard choices over fighting the vallorn in Liathaven. Gunnbrand Ironwill's mandate, the only one upheld in the Spring Synod, permanently changed how Wintermark makes war. Marcher friars sought help laying ghosts in the Greensward, and Feni raiders troubled Hahnmark and the Mournwold. The Brass Coast was unsettled by orc invasions and the Iron Confederacy's attack in Feroz. Urizen continued to endorse the Sword scholars gathering in Morrow. Highguard was offered white granite projects. The Imperial Orcs faced questions of identity. The Senate's ban on bite was enforced across the League, and a Thule party apparently found an ancient orichalcum mine in northern Varushka.

n.Highguard: The Highborn assembly's four statements of principle drew responses, and Highguard was offered three white granite opportunities: roads for pilgrims, the renewal of an old meeting hall, and a chance for benefactors to practise what they preach. Severin von Holberg's encyclical continued to be debated.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were described as approaching a crossroads, facing the unavoidable questions of who they are and what they want, with some possible answers explored.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: Liathaven, which the Jotun held, was where the Navarr were weighing a fight against the vallorn, and former Jotun thralls settled in the Marches were noted.
n.Navarr: The Navarr faced hard choices over the opportunity to fight the vallorn in Liathaven, with their assembly's guidance producing mixed results. They were also concerned with developments among the orc nations.
n.The Brass Coast: Resilient after invasions by two barbarian orc nations, the Freeborn traded gossip about fiery skies over Madruga, earthquakes in Segura and the defence of the City of a Thousand Sails. The Iron Confederacy's attack on Suranni rebels in Feroz stirred growing concern.
n.The Marches: The Marchers faced hauntings in the Greensward, Feni raids in the Mournwold and Alderly, troubling Spring Equinox developments that angered the landskeepers, and stories of Good Walder linked to a stand of miraculous apple trees.
n.Thule: Scouts reported signs that a Thule adventuring party had briefly visited a storm-revealed site in northern Varushka, and the Thule are now likely aware of an ancient orichalcum mine there.
n.Urizen: The Urizen National Assembly continued to endorse the Sword scholars, an old heretical Wisdom sect following the proscribed paragon Sulemaine, who were gathering in Morrow and might yet be reconciled.
n.Varushka: A storm in northern Varushka had uncovered an ossuary, a possibly haunted cave in Brez, a Terunael orichalcum mine and old castle foundations, and the Thule now likely know of the mine. The Roads of Karsk were praised as a success.
n.Wintermark: Gunnbrand Ironwill's upheld mandate, together with the consecration of Kallavesa's marshes, permanently changed how Wintermark armies fight and opened opportunities for the Fist of the Mountain and the Green Shields. Feni raiders also troubled Hahnmark.

t.Feroz: The previous season's brutal Iron Confederacy attack on Suranni rebels sheltering in Feroz caused rising concern and debate across the Brass Coast.
t.Hahnmark: Feni raiders were active in Hahnmark, stealing perishable goods, and possible solutions were being discussed.
t.Kallavesa: The consecration of the marshes of Kallavesa, combined with Gunnbrand Ironwill's mandate, helped open opportunities for Wintermark's generals and change how its armies make war.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: the Roads of Karsk were cited as a success that inspired a civil service survey of new road networks.
t.Liathaven: Liathaven offered the Navarr an opportunity to fight the vallorn there, prompting hard choices guided by their national assembly.
t.Madruga: Fiery displays in the skies over Madruga were among the subjects of Freeborn gossip.
t.Morrow: The Sword scholars, a heretical sect of Wisdom devotees following Sulemaine, were gathering in the foothills of Morrow.
t.Mournwold: The Mournwold was broadly improving, but Spring Equinox developments angered the landskeepers. The territory also suffered Feni raiding and hauntings in the Greensward.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the Ambassador to Otkodov was among those tagged on news of the orc nations.
t.Segura: Earthquakes struck Segura, and the descendants of the paragon Zemress there were the first to voice concern over the Iron Confederacy's attack in Feroz.

r.Mournwold/Alderly: Feni were alleged to be living secretly in the forest of Alderly, their purpose unknown.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Soured by the deaths of tens of thousands, the Greensward was beset by hauntings. Friars based at Honour's Rest were using liao to lay the ghosts to rest but needed help.

382YE Summer Solstice winds of war.d: Fifty surrendered Grendel, including their commander Innevia, were penned on Mariposa awaiting a decision on their fate. Over fifteen thousand Jotun and Lasambrian orcs took most of Serra Damata, held back only by Fort Braydon, while the Corazón raided Kahraman's Bourse seats. In Spiral the Empire held Apstrus, Ateri and three-fifths of Apulus, and captured the Asavean Leri Tarquinius with fifteen wains of white granite. In Sermersuaq some sixty thousand Jotun defeated the Imperial armies at the Ford of Berusen, the shores of the Akonartoq and Atalaq. Around 2,500 Imperial soldiers died there and Senator Atte lost his seat. The Black Plateau's malign influence also grew stronger.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South marched to Sermersuaq from Astolat in the east.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: there was no news from Zenith or the Barrens this season.
n.Grendel: The Grendel lost Madruga and their fort at Apulian, and the Iron Helms hanged their surviving soldiers. Their last troops in Spiral clung to the Clavidian Wilds, and an Asavean Tarquinius was found to have been trading white granite and slaves to them.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Summer Storm secured Ateri and helped storm Apulian, though its orcs lost control in groups under the Plateau's influence. Imperial orcs also fought among the independent soldiers marching with the Bounders in Sermersuaq.
n.Jotun: The Jotun reinvaded Kahraman, taking most of Serra Damata. In Sermersuaq the King of Narkyst and the Jotun Queen led around sixty thousand orcs to victory, taking Sealtoq and Atalaq while honouring the Imperial dead.
n.Navarr: Two large conjunctions to the Green Maw, a Spring regio in Liathaven's Westwood, were detected for the Saturday evening of the Solstice, with skirmishes aimed at Navarr expected there.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn sailors ferried the Drakes to free Madruga, but the Jotun overran much of Serra Damata while the Corazón raided caravans, mines and mana sites across Kahraman. The Fire of the South fought and lost dead in Sermersuaq.
n.The League: The two League armies, the Wolves of War and the Towerjacks, helped push through Apstrus and Ateri to Apulus. The League was the only nation not represented among the independent soldiers fighting with the Bounders.
n.The Marches: The Drakes cleared the Grendel from Atalaya and now hold fifty prisoners. The Tusks and the Bounders marched from Liathaven to Sermersuaq and fought at the Ford of Berusen, the Akonartoq and Atalaq.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule hold the Silver Peaks of Sermersuaq, and their help may be needed to move mithril out if East Floes falls.
n.Urizen: Apstrus and Ateri were liberated and the Citadel Guard is no longer at risk of disbanding. However, freed slaves reported that Urizeni magicians had been shipped south to Grendel slave markets.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark lost Sermersuaq and the Suaq heartland of Atalaq, Senator Atte lost his seat, and the nation's ability to supply armies fell by one. The Bloodcloaks and the Fist of the Mountain fought the Jotun with conspicuous honour.

t.Astolat: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South set out from Astolat on its march north to Sermersuaq.
t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: Grendel soldiers at Apulian threw themselves into the Bay rather than face the Iron Helms.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: the Tusks and Bounders marched north through its fens, and Bregaslanders among the Bounders used the lake waters to their advantage.
t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the Fist of the Mountain marched out of Hahnmark, and the Jotun pursued the Imperial host onto the plains beneath its mountains.
t.Kahraman: Jotun, Hierro and other Lasambrian orcs captured all of Serra Damata except Damata and the Damatian Cliffs. The Corazón raided across the territory, cutting Bourse production and threatening all personal resources if the raids continue.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: Imperial armies marched through its marshes, and recent events there let Wintermark sustain its three armies despite losing Sermersuaq.
t.Liathaven: The Tusks and Bounders left their battle against the vallorn here to march north. Two conjunctions to the Green Maw regio in the Westwood were detected for the Solstice.
t.Madruga: Madruga is entirely in Imperial hands again after the Grendel garrison of Atalaya surrendered, and fifty prisoners are being held at Imperial expense until dealt with.
t.Mareave: Grendel fleeing towards Mareave were slaughtered by maddened bands in Apulus. Imperial armies can only enter through Apstrus, but a spy network could be commissioned via the high passes.
t.Mitwold: Mentioned in passing: the Drakes' general ended his orders with the cry "Mitwold town Forever!"
t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: its haunted ruins are listed among the places where the Jotun have fought the Empire.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: the orcs of Otkodov were recalled as having contended with the Empire over the Silver Peaks three years ago.
t.Reinos: The Jotun invasion of Kahraman was launched from the hills of Reinos, with over fifteen thousand orcs crossing the border three weeks after the Spring Equinox.
t.Sermersuaq: The Jotun took Sealtoq and Atalaq and now hold three regions, leaving the Empire just East Floes, Suaq Fount and the Suaq Wastes. The territory is no longer Imperial and its Senate seat is lost.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun drove the Empire towards the mountains of Skarsind, and withdrawal through Pakaanan's Pass was discussed.
t.Spiral: The Empire now controls Apstrus and Ateri and three-fifths of Apulus, but the Black Plateau's influence has intensified. Armies fighting there next season will suffer heavier casualties and attrition.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the Fire of the South passed through Temeschwar on its way to Sermersuaq.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: there was no news from the Barrens this season.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: there was no news from Zenith this season.

r.Kahraman/Gambit: Mentioned in passing: without Fort Braydon's garrison the Jotun might have pushed on into Gambit.
r.Kahraman/Jade Range: Mentioned in passing: not named directly, though Corazón raiding bands ranged across the whole of Kahraman.
r.Kahraman/Serra Briante: Corazón raiders struck caravans from the Great Mine of Briante, costing it two wains of mithril next season. The region is judged the Jotun's likeliest next target.
r.Kahraman/Serra Damata: The Jotun claimed everything of note except Damata and the Damatian Cliffs, which lost four wains of white granite to raids. Competa del Bosque, a vital Jotun supply line in the south of the region, was named as a Solstice conjunction.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Two conjunctions opening in quick succession to the Green Maw, a Spring regio deep in the Westwood, were detected for the Solstice's Saturday evening.
r.Madruga/Free Landing: Fifty Grendel prisoners, including their commander Innevia, are penned on the island of Mariposa. Innevia revealed they had been ordered to hold Atalaya and Free Landing for a returning armada that never came.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: The Imperial armies were driven back into East Floes and set up a base at Wreck. Here the Jotun Queen returned 270 Imperial dead, laid out with honour.
r.Sermersuaq/Sealtoq: The Jotun won the battles of the Ford of Berusen, the Akonartoq shores and Atalaq to conquer the region. Refugees trapped at Firehand's Taiga were named as a Solstice conjunction.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: Mentioned in passing: the region remains in Thule hands, which matters for moving mithril should East Floes fall.
r.Sermersuaq/Stark: Mentioned in passing: Stark had already been captured by the Jotun before this season's fighting.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Fount: The Jotun Queen tried to flank Atalaq by marching via the Suaq Fount, but was met by the Bounders and the Fire of the South. The region remains in Imperial hands.
r.Sermersuaq/Suaq Wastes: Mentioned in passing: the Suaq Wastes is one of the three regions the Empire still holds in Sermersuaq.
r.Sermersuaq/Tanikipari: Jotun kirkja captured the Hot Springs of Taniki at the Spring Equinox and secured the whole region within a week.
r.Skarsind/Pakaanan's Pass: Mentioned in passing: withdrawing east through Pakaanan's Pass was discussed as the Jotun advanced.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: Imperial forces captured Solen's Doubt and the region. Apstrus is the only route by which an army can enter Mareave.
r.Spiral/Apulus: Apulian fell after a week-long siege, freeing slaves and an Asavean captive, but two-fifths of Apulus remains held by maddened bands. The last Grendel hold the Clavidian Wilds, a Solstice conjunction.
r.Spiral/Ateri: The Summer Storm secured the hills of Ateri, the ruins of Fort Mezudan and the eastern end of the Onyx Path.
r.Spiral/Screed: The horror at the heart of Screed continued to intensify, and the remnants of the howling maniacs once clustered there now roam southern Apulus.

Amend Memorial Gardens of Treji.d: Proposed by the senator for Hercynia and seconded by Skarsind, the motion amended the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens of Treji so that it became an Imperial Orc national title, appointed by the Imperial Orc senators and revocable by the Imperial Orc national assembly. The motion's text framed it as a gesture of friendship, honouring those who fell in the costly liberation of Hercynia. The motion passed, though its outcome remained pending scrutiny. The incumbent was likely to keep the title until they died, stepped down or were revoked. The motion is only constitutional if the title is now revocable by the Imperial Orc national assembly rather than the Navarr one.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs gained the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens of Treji as a national title, to be appointed by their senators and revocable by their national assembly, in recognition of their part in liberating Hercynia.
n.Navarr: Navarr gave up the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens of Treji as a national title, with its Hercynia senator proposing the transfer to the Imperial Orcs as a gesture of friendship.

t.Hercynia: Hercynia's senator proposed the motion, which honours the costly joint Navarr and Imperial Orc liberation of the territory by placing the Memorial Gardens of Treji title in orc hands.

An ideal for living.d: A month after the Spring Equinox, half a dozen sword scholar sects, including the Five Blade Fellowship, the Steel Crane and the Red Scroll Bearers, met amid fractious debates and duels. They had been nearly bled dry fighting Grendel and Druj invaders on their own, and shared reverence for Sulemaine forged a consensus. Rebuilding the temple would need a Senate motion or Wayleave, 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns. It would create a sinecure worth 8 liao and 16 Synod votes, but only if the Urizen Assembly appointed the holder and granted the mysterious Labyrinth Sword. Follow-up mandates could make mandates depend on greater majorities. Some priests instead condemned the scholars as followers of a false paragon.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: in the in-character story, a Dawnish knight named Leo duels the sword scholar Talitha of the Tempests in Morrow, watched by a crowd of his companions.
n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the sword scholar sects had been nearly bled dry fighting Druj invaders, and Zenith is described as being in enemy hands.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel are named alongside the Druj as invaders whom the sword scholars had exhausted themselves fighting.
n.Urizen: Urizen's sword scholars returned to the fold after the National Assembly's judgement, and Urizen was offered the chance to rebuild the Temple of the Winds. If the Assembly also appointed the envoy and secured the Labyrinth Sword, mandates from any assembly would struggle to affect Urizen without a greater majority in the Synod.

t.Morrow: The sword scholars gathered in Morrow at the ruins of the Temple of the Winds, which could be rebuilt there as a new centre for the Wisdom sects.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: a Urizen healer in the story says no life may be squandered while Zenith is still in the hands of the enemy.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Peregro hosted the sword scholar gathering at the ruined Temple of the Winds, once the Disciples of the Tempest Jade Maiden's largest temple, which could be reconstructed as a symbol of reconciliation.

Appoint Dean of the Academy Summer 382YE.d: The motion to appoint the Dean of the Academy was proposed by the senator for Mitwold and seconded by Mournwold. Mitwold escalated the vote so that the election was held immediately. The candidate was elected by constitutional vote and the appointment was ratified by the Throne. As a result, Morana was appointed Dean of the Academy.

n.The Marches: Marcher senators for Mitwold and Mournwold proposed and seconded the motion, and Mitwold's escalation brought about the immediate election of a new Dean of the Academy.

t.Mitwold: Mitwold's senator proposed the motion and escalated the vote so that the election of the Dean was held at once.

Archive:382YE Summer Solstice Imperial t.d: Empress Lisabetta sat on the Throne and also commanded the League of the Quiet Step through her power as Defender of the Empire. The record named every territorial senator, with Upwold's seat vacant, alongside Senate advisors, ambassadors, commissioners, sinecures and ministries. Several trade envoy posts were still to be confirmed. It also listed each nation's generals, the Warmage, Quartermaster General and Imperial Fleet Master. The Synod section covered the cardinals, gatekeepers, virtue inquisitors and other religious posts. The Conclave section named the archmagi and grandmasters. The Bourse section gave seat holders with their bids, though the Damatian Cliffs awaited allocation. The Senate auctioned three Imperial wayleaves that season.

n.Dawn: Dawn held the senatorships of Astolat, Semmerholm and Weirwater, fielded four generals including Tancred de Rondell of the Hounds of Glory, and held the Ambition and Courage cardinalships.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named on the page; it is linked only through Spiral, for which the record still lists a senator, Tanwyn Ankarien, among Urizen's seats.
n.Highguard: Highguard held four senatorships, three generals including Brother Lucifer of the Valiant Pegasus, the Wisdom cardinalship and numerous Synod and Conclave posts.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs held Skarsind's senatorship through Irontide Vio, the generalships of the Winter Sun and Summer Storm, and the Cardinal of the Way through Atla.
n.Navarr: Navarr held three senatorships, the Warmage post and the generalship of the Black Thorns, while the League of the Quiet Step was commanded by the Empress as Defender of the Empire.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast held all four of its senatorships and the generalships of the Red Wind Corsairs and Fire of the South, and Esteban i Del Rio Blanco i Guerra served as Imperial Fleet Master.
n.The League: The League provided the Empress, four senators and two generals, and held the Pride, Prosperity and Vigilance cardinalships.
n.The Marches: The Marches fielded four generals and held senators for Bregasland, Mitwold and Mournwold, but Upwold's seat stood vacant.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Wintermark national Bourse seat of the Stonefield Ice Caves is recorded as held by the Thule.
n.Urizen: Urizen was listed with senators for Morrow, Redoubt and Spiral, and Nicassia Avicia of Phoenix Reach commanded the Citadel Guard.
n.Varushka: Varushka held four senatorships, three generals including Magnus Prochnost of the Iron Helms, and the post of High Bard of the Empire.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark held the senatorships of Hahnmark and Kallavesa, three generals including Lofyn Bloodcloak, and the Loyalty cardinalship, though its Stonefield Ice Caves seat was held by the Thule.

Authorise Ambassador to Axos.d: Proposed by the senator for Weirwater and seconded by the senator for Necropolis, the motion allowed the Ambassador to Axos to offer Axos access to the spy network in the Mountains of the Moon, inviting Axou troops to support it. The motion passed, giving the Ambassador the Senate's backing in issuing the invitation to Axos. The page records only the authorisation and says nothing of whether Axos accepted.

t.Mountains of the Moon: The Imperial spy network in this Tsark-held territory was the focus of the motion, with the Senate backing an invitation for Axou troops to support it.

Blood and gold.d: The General Assembly had declared the vallorn the greatest spiritual threat to the Empire, but the Empire's wars took precedence and the opportunity in Liathaven was likely to pass. Morgan of Brock Bottom Steading argued that a testimony was poor thanks for Marcher losses. He proposed a Navarr-built wayhouse in Upwold, stocked by a national mandate, to give the Marches a permanent herb sinecure. He also suggested ceding the Treji Memorial Gardens to the Imperial Orcs. Weirwood from the Thimble might resupply the Black Thorns if emergency resupply were permitted. Proposed mandates could pressure Imperial and Urizen units to fight in Liathaven. The Constitutional Court rejected Magistrate Abraham's challenge to the testimony judgement.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: the Urizen Assembly said reclaiming Zenith from the Druj must not come at the expense of fighting the vallorn.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step had once aided the Highborn in plague-stricken Reikos, and a Highborn magistrate unsuccessfully challenged the Navarr testimony judgement.
n.Imperial Orcs: Morgan suggested the Senate make the Keeper of the Memorial Gardens at Treji an Imperial Orc appointment, as real thanks for the Summer Storm's help in retaking Hercynia and to win orc support against the vallorn.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: neither the Military Council nor the Throne seemed inclined to campaign in Liathaven, even to retake it from the Jotun.
n.Navarr: The Navarr lacked the support to exploit the vallorn's weakness, with the Quiet Step under the Empress's command and the Black Thorns close to breaking. They were offered ways to win allies, including herb sacrifices, ceding the Treji gardens and pushing a General Assembly or Assembly of the Nine mandate.
n.The Marches: The Marchers had borne most of nearly fifteen hundred deaths in Liathaven. Their armies had withdrawn, and Morgan proposed a Navarr-built Upwold wayhouse to give Marcher farmers a permanent sinecure of 30 herbs a season.
n.Urizen: The Urizen Assembly declared that the fight against the vallorn in Liathaven should take precedence over liberating Zenith. A proposed mandate would cost Urizen units two ranks of morale if they did not support an Imperial army in Liathaven.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: cited as an example of gratitude for giving Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs in thanks for the Crown of Three Tears.

t.Hercynia: Mentioned in passing: Morgan's steading lies deep in Hercynia, and the Summer Storm's help in retaking the territory was cited as a debt poorly repaid.
t.Liathaven: A rare window to fight the vallorn in Liathaven was closing, with no Navarr army there and the Marcher armies withdrawn. Proposed mandates sought to draw Imperial and Urizen forces back to fight there.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the Quiet Step had fought in Reikos when it was plague-stricken, to help the Highborn.
t.Skarsind: Mentioned in passing: cited as Wintermark's gift to the Imperial Orcs in thanks for the return of the Crown of Three Tears.
t.Therunin: The Thimble weirwood forest in Therunin, still producing 20 wains a season under Idris Eternal, was suggested as the source for resupplying the Black Thorns and funding Morgan's proposals.
t.Upwold: Morgan proposed a Navarr wayhouse in Upwold, costing 15 wains of weirwood and 30 crowns. Backed by a Navarr mandate, it would become a Marcher-appointed sinecure producing 30 herbs a season.
t.Zenith: The Urizen Assembly judged that liberating Zenith from the Druj should wait while the chance to fight the vallorn in Liathaven was seized.

Both cut alike.d: Druj reconnaissance bands from Zenith were scouting Redoubt, Morrow and Spiral. The Jotun were closing on Atalaq in Sealtoq, and four conjunctions to the Nuajaat Shore could protect fleeing Suaq refugees. Strange Navarr-like warriors travelling with heralds of Yaw'nagrah threatened a Spring regio at Eleri's Paths in Brocéliande. Warriors in Kallavesa were dragging Suaq captives beneath the Gullet. Feni raiders troubled Hahnmark. Navarr vates could attempt high-magnitude rituals at the Verdant Maw in Westwood, which Surut wished to see turned into a Winter regio. Two storm-damaged Grendel ships had come aground in Sarvos and Necropolis, and their marines were pillaging the coast.

n.Druj: Elite Druj bands bearing beetle banners crossed from Zenith to scout Redoubt, Morrow and Spiral, avoiding citadels and fights, and five conjunctions offered the chance to stop them reporting back.
n.Grendel: Two storm-damaged Grendel ships came aground at Haven Rocks and White Sands. Their marines pillaged farms, smelters and woodmills while gathering repair materials, and they could now be intercepted.
n.Highguard: Highguard was named as interested in the Druj incursions into Redoubt. Grendel marines had pillaged the land around White Sands in Necropolis, offering Highborn a chance for revenge.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs were named as interested in countering the Druj scouts in Redoubt and Spiral, where they had campaign armies.
n.Jotun: Jotun forces were tightening their ring around Atalaq, offering everyone the Choice and taking children as thralls. Four conjunctions offered the chance to intercept their warbands on the Nuajaat Shore.
n.Navarr: Navarr vates had chances to defend a Spring regio at Eleri's Paths and cast the Dance of Navarr and Thorn there. They could also attempt planned high-magnitude rituals at the Verdant Maw in Westwood, where a herald of Surut would await them.
n.The League: Grendel marines pillaged near Orphan's Haven in Sarvos, and the League was named among the nations with campaign armies in Spiral facing the Druj scouts.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: Marchers of the North Fens were telling tales of shapeshifting beasts in the Gullet that devour fisherfolk.
n.Urizen: Druj scouts roamed the Urizen territories of Redoubt, Morrow and Spiral that neighbour Zenith. Sentinels were readied against them, and conjunctions offered the chance to deny the Druj knowledge of the terrain.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka was named among the nations with campaign armies in Spiral with an interest in the Druj scouts.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark faced several threats: Jotun closing on Atalaq's refugees in Sealtoq, warriors dragging Suaq captives into the Gullet from Kallavesa, and Feni raiders damaging farms, businesses and herb gardens in Hahnmark.

t.Bay of Catazar: Two Grendel vessels, apparently battered by a storm in deeper water, made landfall on the northern coast of the bay.
t.Bregasland: Mentioned in passing: Marchers from Bregasland spoke of shapeshifting beasts in the Gullet.
t.Brocéliande: Courageous Bough vates were defending a Spring regio at Eleri's Paths against strange Navarr-like warriors and heralds of Yaw'nagrah. Conjunctions there offered a chance to repair the territory's trods.
t.Hahnmark: Feni raiding troubled Hahnmark, and two conjunctions offered the chance to halve or wholly remove the harm to Winterfolk farms, businesses and herb gardens.
t.Kallavesa: A band of warriors attacked wandering groups along the coast and dragged Suaq captives into the Gullet, and a conjunction offered a chance to stop further kidnappings.
t.Liathaven: Conjunctions reached the Verdant Maw, a Spring regio deep in vallorn-infested Liathaven, where visitors risked Green Lung and Surut sought to claim the regio.
t.Morrow: Druj scouts were active in Morrow, and conjunctions to the Weaving Wood and Green Road Citadel offered chances to stop them.
t.Necropolis: Grendel marines from a ship aground at White Sands pillaged nearby farms, smelters and woodmills and were trying to refloat their vessel.
t.Redoubt: Druj reconnaissance parties moved through eastern Redoubt, with conjunctions to the Beggar's Trail and the Trees on the Mountain of Aquina.
t.Sarvos: A Grendel ship foundered at Haven Rocks, and its marines raided the surrounding area for supplies.
t.Spiral: Druj scouts were active near the Twilight Gate, and a conjunction to the Wooden Rest of Dusk offered a chance to intercept them.
t.Zenith: The Druj reconnaissance bands set out from Zenith to scout the Urizen territories bordering it.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: Mentioned in passing: Marchers of the North Fens were already telling tales of shapeshifting Gullet beasts.
r.Brocéliande/Elerael: At Eleri's Paths, near Brackensong Steading, two conjunctions led to a Spring regio that the Courageous Bough were warding against heralds of Yaw'nagrah.
r.Hahnmark/Southridge: The Frayed Talons of Dusk were fleeing pursuing Feni after a failed ambush, and a conjunction to Whitethorn Gulch offered a chance to intervene.
r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: A Feni warband beaten back from a Steinr hall was camped near the ruins of Eafshal, where a conjunction allowed it to be defeated.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: A conjunction to Hval Beach offered a chance to stop the warriors who had been dragging Suaq captives into the Gullet.
r.Liathaven/West Ranging: Mentioned in passing: the withdrawal of Imperial armies from West Ranging made intelligence on the Verdant Maw hard to obtain.
r.Liathaven/Westwood: Two conjunctions led to the Verdant Maw, a Spring regio where Navarr vates could cast rituals and a herald of Surut would wait to receive it if it became a Winter regio.
r.Morrow/Operus: Druj scouts were active in the Weaving Wood and near the Green Road Citadel by Canterspire, where Saturday conjunctions opened.
r.Necropolis/Longbeach: A Grendel ship ran aground at White Sands, and its marines pillaged the area before trying to refloat their vessel.
r.Redoubt/Limus: A conjunction to the Trees on the Mountain of Aquina, across a valley from the Granite Pillar's camp, offered a chance to intercept Druj scouts.
r.Redoubt/Willstone: A conjunction to the Beggar's Trail, near the Winter Sun's camp, offered a chance to intercept Druj scouts.
r.Sarvos/Riposi: A Grendel ship foundered at Haven Rocks, east of Orphan's Haven, and its marines raided local farms and works.
r.Spiral/Ossuary: Druj scouts were active near the Twilight Gate, with a conjunction to the Wooden Rest of Dusk.
r.Zenith/Iteri: Mentioned in passing: the Druj bands crossed the open plains of Iteri on their way out of Zenith.

Bury the hatchet.d: Meraud agreed to discuss a ritual with Archmage Solomon and asked to meet Enchantress Vandale, Carlos Guerra, the Eternal Family and the Concordium of Pallas. The Whisper Gallery, though enmitied and still at war, would treat with Night Archmage Elyssiathain only if Ancel Watcher met the Cardinals of the Sanguine Icon privately. Callidus charged for its message, fixed a trade-focused agenda and summoned Estana i Mestiere i Guerra. Sinokenon required a representative of the Throne. Llofir warned of retribution if its herald Pah Rashet were harmed. Skathe would discuss cursing those who despoiled Spiral, her home, and awaited a gift. A timetable set each parley.

n.Dawn: The Whisper Gallery addressed the Night Archmage as a "sweet witch of Dawn" and demanded the witch Ancel Steward meet their Cardinals alone, while Meraud asked to speak with Enchantress Vandale of House Vandale about a gift.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named, but Skathe's parley concerns cursing those responsible for despoiling Spiral, which Grendel held at the time.
n.Urizen: Skathe of the Thrice-cursed Court agreed to discuss with the Winter Archmage laying a vengeful curse on those who despoiled her home, the Urizen territory of Spiral, and offered to speak with a Highborn chapter with a red torch if the archmage supported them.

t.Spiral: Spiral is named as Skathe's home, and her parley with Winter Archmage Emilia Ankarien was to concern a vengeful curse on those responsible for despoiling it while it was held by Grendel.

Civil tongue.d: Sumaah, still at war, sent Envoy Azcan and Tipoa the Insightful back to request a formal Senate reception from Ambassador Accalon of Felix's Watch, with Tarquinius of Ankarien present; otherwise they would leave. Asavea stayed warm but faced provincial revolts and sought mercenaries. Jarm's Rigia stayed closed, and the Kobarid offered star jewels through a proposed fortified exchange, with a deadline of the Autumn Equinox. Faraden trade grew with Segura's new roads. Axos offered 500 scouts for the Mountains of the Moon spy network, which needs a Military Council or Senate vote. The Suranni demanded an end to liao smuggling and spoke of reparations. Cargo's fortification against the Druj was half complete.

n.Dawn: Faraden merchants remained keen on a trade enclave in central Astolat, ideally at Laroc or Oldheart, to reach Dawnish luxuries, though nothing had yet been arranged.
n.Druj: Cargo, home to three embassies, was under immediate threat of Druj invasion, and its foreign-aided fortification was half built to resist them.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Sarcophan discontent over the Delves' agreement with the Grendel continued, though it was muted by the magic protecting Imperial ships.
n.Highguard: With the completion of the Necropolis warehouses, more Sarcophan merchants came to Highguard, and the Kruidenkenner herbalists' guild sought new markets through its enclave there.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: Sumaah delegate Tipoa the Insightful was noted as best known for work on doctrine changes concerning the Imperial Orcs.
n.The Brass Coast: New roads brought prosperity to Segura and wealth to Madruga through Faraden trade, while Asavean merchants grew common on the coast. Kalino's troops left Feroz after the slave rebellion was crushed, but the Suranni accused the Empire of smuggling liao through Feroz.
n.The League: Asavean merchants were increasingly seen across Sarvos, the new Faraden road reached Tassato, and the Kobarid, hosted by Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato, proposed an exchange modelled on Tassato's Mana Exchange.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the civil service Secretary to the Diplomatic Corps, John Cooper of Upwold, double-checked Sumaah's request for Tarquinius of Ankarien to attend.
n.Urizen: Axos sought a land route to the spires of eastern Urizen and offered to help map the Mountains of the Moon, an offer that would need Military Council or Senate approval.
n.Varushka: Faraden traders remained eager for an enclave in Volodmartz, most likely Triosk, to gain access to Varushkan timber and ore, though there had been no movement on it.

t.Astolat: The Faraden hoped for a trade enclave in central Astolat, at Laroc or Oldheart, but nothing had yet been agreed.
t.Bay of Catazar: The recent Imperial effort to map the Bay angered the Iron Confederacy, which talked of reparations for the incursion into its coastal waters.
t.Feroz: Kalino's troops withdrew from Feroz after the slave rebellion was crushed, and the Temple of Balo and the Black Bull prospered. The Suranni, however, demanded an end to alleged liao smuggling through the territory.
t.Kalino: The Duke of Kalino's troops returned south across the border after helping crush the slave rebellion in Feroz.
t.Madruga: The new road through Siroc linked Segura's network to the Blood Red Roads, and the influx of Faraden merchants brought more wealth into Madruga.
t.Mountains of the Moon: Axos offered 500 Agema and Toxatai scouts to support the Imperial spy network mapping the territory, provided the Military Council or Senate approved. Any maps produced would be shared with the Axou.
t.Necropolis: The completed warehouses drew more Sarcophan merchants, including the Kruidenkenner herbalists, who were keen to exploit their new Highguard enclave.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: Asavean merchants were described as increasingly common across Sarvos.
t.Segura: The completed south-western road network, linking Anduz to Tassato via Siroc, brought increased prosperity to Segura through Faraden trade.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Zana noted that no map showed any mountain pass from Spiral towards Axos.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato was named as an endpoint of the new Faraden road and as the model for the Kobarid's proposed exchange.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: only as the home of civil servant John Cooper of Upwold.
t.Volodmartz: The Faraden remained keen on a trade enclave in Volodmartz, most likely at Triosk, for timber and ore, though nothing had progressed.
t.Zenith: Mentioned in passing: in the story, Zana observed that no map showed any pass from Zenith through the eastern mountains.

Claim Sungold Pass.d: Proposed by the senator for Karov and seconded by the senator for Sarvos, the motion reasserted the Empire's claim that the Sungold Pass belongs to Opascari in Volodmartz rather than to neighbouring Otkodov. It also declared that foreigners exploiting resources in Imperial land without the Empire's direct invitation is not acceptable. The motion passed. It had implications for the Thule, who may also have laid claim to the mine there. The claim did not last: at the Summer Solstice 383YE the Senate chose to cede Sungold Pass to the Thule, effectively abrogating this motion.

n.Thule: The Senate rejected any Thule right to exploit the Sungold Pass mine without Imperial invitation, challenging their possible claim. A year later the Senate ceded the pass to them.
n.Varushka: Varushka's claim to the Sungold Pass as part of its territory of Volodmartz was formally upheld by the Senate, though the pass was ceded to the Thule a year later.

t.Otkodov: The Thule-held territory of Otkodov was explicitly denied possession of the Sungold Pass, which the Senate insisted lay within the Empire.
t.Volodmartz: The Senate declared the Sungold Pass and the Traveller part of Volodmartz and condemned unsanctioned foreign exploitation of its resources there.

r.Volodmartz/Opascari: Opascari was named as the region containing the Sungold Pass and the mountain called the Traveller. That claim was effectively abandoned when the pass was ceded to the Thule in Summer 383YE.

Construct Autumn's Boon.d: Proposed by Kallavesa and seconded by Casinea, the motion commissions a mana sinecure named Autumn's Boon, to be built in Wood Heath in Hahnmark at standard cost. Its holder, the Collector of Prosperity's Boon, is to be selected by the Senators of Wintermark. The motion passed in principle but left the size of the sinecure unspecified, a necessary detail for the senator to determine. After the Summer Solstice 382YE, Tyr Brennan provided 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns towards construction. Once complete, the sinecure will create the Imperial title.

n.Wintermark: The Senators of Wintermark are to select the Collector of Prosperity's Boon, giving the nation control of a new mana sinecure on its own land in Hahnmark.

t.Hahnmark: Hahnmark is to gain a mana sinecure, Autumn's Boon, towards which Tyr Brennan supplied 12 wains of mithril and 24 crowns after the Summer Solstice.

r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Wood Heath is the chosen site for the Autumn's Boon sinecure, which on completion will create the title of Collector of Prosperity's Boon.

Construct Bleak Tower.d: Proposed by Spiral and seconded by Reikos, the motion took up an opportunity presented at the Spring Equinox. The commission used non-standard costs: 30 wains each of weirwood and white granite, 120 crowns in labour, and six months to complete. Edmundo of Damakan's Forge supplied 10 wains of weirwood, 22 wains of white granite and 8 thrones after the Summer Solstice 382YE. Thalia of Netherwatch provided 20 wains of weirwood, 8 wains of white granite and 7 thrones after the Spring Equinox 383YE. Once complete, the tower spreads a share of 80 random herbs through Morrow's herb gardens. It also creates the title Custodian of the Bleak Tower, appointed by Urizen senators, which receives six doses of heart's blood each season.

n.Urizen: Urizen gains a great work that shelters Pallas's displaced herbalists and enriches its herb gardens in Morrow. Its senators appoint the new Custodian of the Bleak Tower.

t.Morrow: Morrow becomes home to the Bleak Tower, which distributes a share of 80 random herbs through the territory's herb gardens.

r.Morrow/Ravion: Ravion is the site of the Bleak Tower, which houses the refugees and researchers of the herb garden of Pallas.

Construct Cinderpath Exchange.d: Proposed by the senator for Necropolis and seconded by Redoubt, the motion would have created the Cinderpath Exchange and the Imperial title 'Cinderpath Benefactor', an opportunity presented by the benefactors of Highguard. It was rejected. Scrutiny found that Abraham had given incorrect information in the Senate about its effect on white granite at public auction. With the Highborn assembly mandate supporting it, the ministry would have removed 6 wains of white granite each season from the auction, rising to 8 if the General Assembly mandate were later passed. The civil service raised an administrative motion to reconsider, but it also failed. A constitutional challenge confirmed the title would have been appointed by vote of Highborn congregations, not the Highborn assembly.

n.Highguard: Highguard lost the chance to control a white granite ministry through the Cinderpath Benefactor title, which a constitutional challenge confirmed would have been chosen by Highborn congregations rather than their National Assembly.

t.Casinea: The Highborn-held territory of Casinea will not gain the Cinderpath Exchange, after both the original motion and the reconsideration failed.

r.Casinea/Mareholm: Mareholm was the proposed site of the Cinderpath Exchange, but no ministry will be built there.

Construct College of Engineering and Arc.d: Proposed by Tassato and seconded by Astolat, the motion arose from an opportunity offered by the eternal Adamant. The college required at least 60 wains of white granite and 120 crowns and six months to build, and had to stand in a hilly region, which in Temeschwar meant Locul. The Master of the Koboldi, appointed through the Conclave, would be Adamant's representative to the Empire and vice versa. Adamant intended the title to announce one extra commission each season using at least 30 wains of white granite, but only if its holder could freely choose what to build. The original wording failed this and was amended at Winter Solstice 382YE. Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato later provided white granite and thrones in 383YE.

n.The League: A League senator, Tassato, proposed the motion, and the college would stand in League-held Temeschwar, with a Tassatan magnate, Cesare Sanguineo Rezia Di Tassato, providing white granite and thrones towards its construction.

t.Temeschwar: Temeschwar was chosen as the site of the new college, which would be ceded to the eternal Adamant once complete.

r.Temeschwar/Locul: As the only hilly region in Temeschwar, Locul was required by Adamant's stipulation to host the college of engineering and architecture.

Construct House of the Proffered Hand.d: Proposed by Semmerholm and seconded by the Conscience, the motion commissioned the House of the Proffered Hand at standard cost: 10 wains of white granite and 20 crowns in labour, taking three months to build. The motion named Winterbourne, but the civil service then learned this region was wrong. Because work had not begun, an administrative motion was raised at the Autumn Equinox, and the Senate confirmed construction at Caer Faucon, a small town in southern Astolat near the Highguard border. Lady Eleanor Novarion supplied the granite and crowns after the Spring Equinox 383YE. The work created the title Lady of the Proffered Hand, held with tenure.

n.Dawn: Dawn gains a new Imperial title, Lady of the Proffered Hand, held for life and appointed by the Dawn National Assembly, with the sinecure built in the Dawn territory of Astolat.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Caer Faucon, the corrected site of the House, is described as lying in southern Astolat near the Highguard border.

t.Astolat: Astolat gains the House of the Proffered Hand, a liao sinecure finally confirmed at Caer Faucon, a small town in the south of the territory.

r.Astolat/Winterbourne: Winterbourne was named as the site in the original motion, but the civil service found this to be an error, and the Senate later confirmed construction at Caer Faucon.

Construct Legacy of Wisdom.d: Announced under an Imperial Wayleave in Summer 382YE, the great work was to cost 40 wains of mithril and 80 crowns of labour, taking three months, and was funded by 'La Volpe' and the Bloody Butchers of Temeschwar. Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar provided 40 wains of mithril and 10 thrones after the Summer Solstice. The Druj invasion of Morrow then destroyed the construction site of the central stellae and several smaller stellae, so all progress was lost and Lorenzo received a partial refund. If Caeli were recaptured before the Summer Solstice 383YE, work could restart from scratch without a new motion or commission. Completed, it would have distributed 37 crystal mana between Morrow's mana sites.

n.Druj: The Druj invasion of Morrow destroyed the construction site, wiping out all progress on the great work.
n.The League: League citizens, Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar with 'La Volpe' and the Bloody Butchers of Temeschwar, funded the work with mithril and thrones, but saw their investment lost and only partly refunded.
n.Urizen: Urizen stood to gain a great work spreading 37 crystal mana across Morrow's mana sites, but lost it to the Druj invasion unless Caeli is recaptured before Summer 383YE.

t.Morrow: The great work's stellae were being raised in Morrow until the Druj invasion destroyed the site; work could restart from scratch if Caeli is retaken before the Summer Solstice 383YE.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: the funders were the Bloody Butchers of Temeschwar and Lorenzo Macelliao von Temeschwar.

Construct Prosperity of Afal.d: Using an Imperial Wayleave, Vilkas Blake commissioned a mana sinecure in Ashrook, Upwold, at standard cost: 10 wains of mithril, 20 crowns of labour and three months to build. He provided both the mithril and the crowns after the Summer Solstice 382YE. Once complete, it creates the Imperial title Guardian of the Prosperity of Afal, appointed by Marcher senators. The announcement wanted the holder to be a citizen of Upwold, but the constitutional ruling noted an Imperial title cannot be restricted that way. It could be made a Marcher national position, and electors remain free to choose only an Upwold citizen.

n.The Marches: Marcher senators will appoint the Guardian of the Prosperity of Afal, a title that may be made a Marcher national position but cannot legally be limited to Upwold citizens.

t.Upwold: A mana sinecure, the Prosperity of Afal, is being built in Ashrook, Upwold, to produce 9 mana each season once complete.

Construct expansion to Halls of Knowledg.d: Proposed by the senator for Morrow and seconded by Miekarova, the motion sought an Autumn wing for the Halls of Knowledge. The civil service costed it at 25 wains each of mithril, white granite and weirwood plus 150 crowns, taking six months. After the Summer Solstice Agrippa provided 25 wains of mithril, 19 of weirwood, 1 of white granite and 12 thrones. The Druj invasion of Morrow then destroyed the Halls, ending all work; Agrippa received a partial refund. Had it been finished, the Provost would have been able to research Autumn magic at 15 ranks a season and spend money to speed that research.

n.Druj: The Druj invasion of Morrow destroyed the Halls of Knowledge, wiping out all progress on the expansion and making the commission impossible to complete.
n.Urizen: Urizen lost both the planned Autumn wing and the Halls of Knowledge themselves to the Druj, along with the Autumn magic research it would have given the Provost.

t.Morrow: Morrow's senator proposed the expansion, but the Druj invasion of the territory destroyed the Halls of Knowledge and ended construction.

r.Morrow/Peregro: Peregro was home to the Halls of Knowledge where the Autumn wing was to be built, and the Halls were destroyed there during the Druj invasion.

Construct the Salt Guard.d: The commission used non-standard costs: 100 wains of white granite, 20 wains of weirwood, 30 Thrones in labour, and an upkeep of 10 Thrones each season. It would take a year to complete. Adan i DelToro i Riqueza, Lieselotte van Holberg and Imperatrix Lisabetta supplied materials and coin over the following seasons. Vigilant citizens inspired by the shrine of the Sentinel in Casinea were to provide 20 wains of white granite and 5 Thrones. The Immaculate Architect ritual was also cast on the project after the Autumn Equinox. Once complete, the Salt Guard would resist conventional invaders anywhere in Madruga with an effective strength of 3,000. Against Shore Offensives aimed at the Siroc Plains, its strength would rise to 6,000.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: citizens inspired by the shrine of the Sentinel in the Highborn territory of Casinea were to contribute granite and Thrones to the build.
n.The Brass Coast: The Brass Coast gains a planned major fortification in Madruga to protect Siroc and the Lyceum from invasion, particularly attacks from the sea.

t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: the shrine of the Sentinel in Casinea inspired vigilant citizens to pledge 20 wains of white granite and 5 Thrones towards the construction.
t.Madruga: The Salt Guard was to be built in Siroc, giving Madruga a defence of strength 3,000 against land invasion anywhere in the territory, and 6,000 against Shore Offensives on the Siroc Plains.

Construct the Thorned Rose.d: The motion, tabled under an Imperial Wayleave by Silvio di Tassato, commissioned a sinecure producing crystal mana at standard cost, with its size left to the bearer of the wayleave to determine. The Thorned Rose was to teach would-be vates what swearing the oath means and guide those wishing to learn of magic and the realms. The Dean would be appointed by the Navarr senators, hold tenure, and swear an oath to train the willing and never accept the Vate Oath of the irresponsible, reckless or unworthy. After the Summer Solstice, Bledri Eternal provided 10 wains of mithril and 20 crowns towards construction. Once completed, the sinecure creates the title Dean of the Thorned Rose.

n.Navarr: The Navarr senators gain the power to appoint a tenured Dean charged with preparing prospective vates for their oath, giving the nation an Imperial institution devoted to the path of the vate.

t.Miaren: The Thorned Rose was to be built just outside Seren in Miaren, establishing a mana-producing seat of learning for vates in the territory.

Create title Custodian of Ivarsgard Dock.d: Proposed by the senator for Karsk and seconded by the Dean of the Academy, the motion took up an offer from the Bedelaar Huisbaas Vak Eck and required no construction or cost. It represents an agreement between a Sarcophan Delves concern and the people of Ivarsgard. The new title is appointed annually at the Spring Equinox by Varushkan citizens who maintain a forest or mine resource. The holder can purchase Cerulean Mazzarine from Sarcophan merchants using the docks on the Semmerlak.

t.The Semmerlak: An area of the Ivarsgard docks on the Semmerlak became a herb ministry, where the new Custodian can buy Cerulean Mazzarine from Sarcophan merchants trading on the lake.

Declare Feni group to be foreigners.d: The motion declared the Feni group calling itself "The Woods That Fell" to be foreigners, and it passed. These are the Feni who fled when the sinkhole opened. At the time there was one large group of them in Hahnmark and another in the Mournwold, and both were still raiding local settlements in those areas. The motion was proposed by the senator for Bregasland and seconded by the senator for Kallavesa.

n.The Marches: The Marcher senator for Bregasland proposed the declaration, which leaves one of the two large groups of raiding Feni, the one in the Marcher-held Mournwold, legally foreign.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's senator for Kallavesa seconded the motion, which applies to one of the two raiding Feni groups, the one sheltering in the Wintermark territory of Hahnmark.

t.Hahnmark: One of the two large groups of "The Woods That Fell" Feni was in Hahnmark and was still raiding local settlements there when it was declared foreign.
t.Mournwold: A large group of "The Woods That Fell" Feni was in the Mournwold and was still raiding local settlements there when it was declared foreign.

Disseminate True Liao visions.d: Proposed by Redoubt and seconded by Madruga on the Spider's Vantage Spire's suggestion, the motion led the Civil Service to distribute Echoes of the Labyrinth abroad. Asavean interest centred on a vision about a Coriolani martyr. Followers of the Way in Jarm, the Commonwealth and the Sarcophan Delves embraced the books, blunting Sumaah missionaries for a time. The Faraden found them popular, but the Ogudai and Modnos families were enraged by portrayals of their kin. Axou priests denounced them. The Sumaah recorded every buyer. Suranni priests burned the books, and in Autumn 382YE the motion was amended to exclude the Iron Confederacy.

n.Dawn: A vision by Collwyn de Rondell of Dawn depicted the Faraden Genghis Modnos as a cowardly villain, which enraged the Modnos family, who may seek vengeance on those they see as liars, and unsettled priests who believe souls are reborn only within a family.
n.Grendel: After the peace treaty the books were made available to the Grendel, but apart from a few collectors the orcs of the Broken Shore showed little interest in foreign humans' past-life visions.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: the motion was proposed by the senator for Redoubt.
n.Thule: Copies sent to the Thule were accepted without comment, and merchants reported that the books were invariably bought in bulk by a handful of polite warlocks.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the distribution followed a suggestion by the Spider's Vantage Spire of Urizen.

t.Bastion: Mentioned in passing: pilgrims abroad valued the volumes as a connection to Bastion, the heart of the faith, against Sumaah missionaries speaking out against it.
t.Otkodov: Echoes of the Labyrinth was sent to Otkodov, where it was accepted without comment and bought in bulk by a few polite warlocks.

Easy come, worth less.d: Absalom's call to fight the Druj in Zenith found a receptive audience, and a backing mandate would penalise Highborn units not supporting the Granite Pillar, Seventh Wave or Valiant Pegasus. Malachi's statement on walking the trods opened proposed mandates to send up to a fifth of Highguard, or citizens of every nation, onto the trods as Navarr or as pilgrims. This would ruin taxes and armies but speed new chances against the vallorn, and would be near-impossible to undo. Sela's spider-jar warning brought weekly harmless jars to Sybella Cross for six weeks. Able's offer of sanctuary drew few Urizen, who stayed in Redoubt and Morrow, but chapters sent supplies.

n.Druj: The Highborn were stirred against the Druj, with a mandate offered to rally the nation behind its armies fighting them in Zenith and beyond.
n.Highguard: Its people heeded calls to fight the Druj, hunt spider jars and aid Urizen refugees. They also faced proposals that could send up to a fifth of the nation onto the trods, at ruinous cost to taxes, businesses and armies.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the nation is not named, though the dwindling chance to take ground from the vallorn in Liathaven, which it held, is referenced.
n.Navarr: Proposed mandates could send tens of thousands of Highborn or Imperial citizens to join the Navarr or walk the trods as pilgrims. Navarr vates judged this equal to adding two to four territories to the trod network.
n.Urizen: Urizen displaced from Zenith were offered sanctuary in Highguard. Most chose to stay in the mountains of their homeland, though they gratefully received food, tools, tents and timber from Highborn chapters.

t.Bastion: A few Urizen with existing ties travelled to friends or family here, and a handful of suspect jars were sent from Bastion to Sybella Cross.
t.Casinea: Mentioned in passing: a handful of worried citizens here also sent jars to Sybella Cross for inspection.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: the opportunity to take ground from the vallorn here was described as dwindling, which a mass trod-walking mandate could more than equal.
t.Morrow: Many Urizen who fled Zenith remained camped in southern Morrow, where Highborn chapters sent supplies to support them.
t.Necropolis: A small number of Urizen with existing connections to Highguard sought sanctuary with friends or family here.
t.Redoubt: Many Urizen refugees stayed camped in northern Redoubt rather than leave their homeland, receiving food, blankets, tents and hardwood from Highborn chapters.
t.Reikos: The spider-jar warning caused consternation here. Scouts combed the land around new chapters and sent jars to Sybella Cross, but none proved dangerous and none appeared near Reikos settlements.
t.Zenith: The Highborn Assembly urged support for liberating Zenith from the Druj, while those who had fled its fall sheltered in Redoubt and Morrow, hoping to return.

r.Bastion/Sybella Cross: Sybella Cross Physician's Hall received weekly shipments of suspected spider jars for about six weeks. All proved to be ordinary jars or natural dead spiders, none cursed or dangerous.

Fight with monsters.d: At the Spring Equinox 382YE the Wintermark Assembly upheld (236–0) a mandate sending Gunnbrand Ironwill with liao to remind the Mark of the hero's path. Any Wintermark army may now fight with honour when attacking, forcing allied Imperial forces alongside it to abandon plunder and butchery and protecting civilians on both sides. Wintermark armies fighting the Jotun now permanently gain more victory but inflict fewer casualties, fighting them as equals in honour. The Rune-bound mystics emerged from Kallavesa to offer the Fist of the Mountains the Farsighted quality, and the Green Shields could become Heroic, each for 25 wains of mithril. Atte Arrow-Tongue Metsastajason and Osric provided the mithril for each respectively.

n.Jotun: Wintermark armies now permanently fight the Jotun as honourable equals, winning ground more readily but slaying significantly fewer Jotun, and recent Jotun actions suggest the change has been noticed.
n.Thule: Mentioned in passing: the Thule gathering in Wintermark's north are cited as one of the threats the Green Shields must stand against.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark has irrevocably committed its armies to heroic traditions, gaining the fight with honour order, permanent honourable tactics against the Jotun, and the Farsighted Fist of the Mountains and Heroic Green Shields, though at the cost of strained cooperation with allied armies using crueller methods.

t.Hahnmark: Mentioned in passing: the reawakening of heroism is described as spreading through the mountains of Hahnmark.
t.Kallavesa: The Rune-bound, a hall of mystics from all three Wintermark traditions who had tended Emperor Guntherm's resting place, emerged from the Kallavesa swamps to rejoin the Fist of the Mountains, and the reawakening of heroism is said to have begun there.
t.Sermersuaq: With Jotun warriors pushing forward across Sermersuaq, the Green Shields' heroic resolve to stand between Wintermark and her enemies is framed as more important than ever there.

Fit and proper.d: At the Spring Equinox 382YE the Conclave refused to reconcile Rivers Run Red, then passed declarations reaffirming virtuous magicians' right to use curses and instructing the Voice of the Quiet Forest to cast the curse on Therunin. Many magicians across the Empire felt this undermined the Conclave's moral authority and implied interdiction could be ignored. Camila i Erigo proposed that the Senate create a Declaration of Endorsement so the Conclave could lawfully approve particular uses, expecting more interdictions as a result. The Constitutional Court saw no objection in principle but needs a clearly worded Senate motion addressing targets, timing, who is endorsed and eternals under enmity, and would not allow open-ended endorsement of individuals. The proposal awaits a senator to take it up.

n.Navarr: Navarr magicians, the Voice of the Quiet Forest, were told by the Conclave to cast the interdicted Rivers Run Red on Therunin, the very defiance of interdiction that sparked the controversy over the Conclave's authority.
n.The Brass Coast: The Freeborn magician Camila i Erigo leads the push for a Declaration of Endorsement, and one of the two contested declarations was raised by Alejandra i Erigo.

t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: Camila i Erigo, the proposal's author, is described as coming from the hills of Kahraman.
t.Therunin: Therunin was the target of the interdicted Rivers Run Red curse that the Conclave instructed the Voice of the Quiet Forest to cast there, prompting the debate on interdiction.

Good apples.d: Following a Marcher Assembly judgement citing a true aura on Bastard Tom of Stoke as Good Walder's inspiration, rumours of the paragon spread across the Marches, and villages decorated old apple trees they claimed were his grave. In the Golden Downs, just south of Hay near the Mourn border, the oldest tree in a copse said to mark Walder's grave, and all its neighbours, became heavy with fruit. The friars proposed a folly (5 wains of white granite, 10 crowns) creating the title Keeper of Good Walder's Grave, or a larger sinecure shrine yielding liao and Synod votes. Alternatively, the site could become an inspirational tomb using true liao. None was commissioned during the Summer Solstice, but the opportunities remain open.

n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Good Walder's lessons are said to be preached in Highguard today.
n.The Marches: Marcher villages across several territories are claiming a part in Walder's story, and the friars of Hay asked that the Marcher Assembly, or at a stretch the Prosperity Assembly, appoint any Keeper of Good Walder's Grave.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Walder's warnings about good hospitality are said to be appreciated as far afield as Varushka.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Walder's stories were told in Wintermark long before there was an Empire.

t.Bregasland: A few places in Bregasland have joined in the rumours, reminding passers-by of their village's part in Walder's story.
t.Mitwold: Mitwold is home to the miraculous apple copse near Hay, where the friars proposed a folly, shrine or memorial to Good Walder, none of which has yet been built.
t.Mournwold: Even a couple of pubs in the Mourn are claiming a part in Walder's story, and the miraculous copse lies near the Mourn border.
t.Upwold: Several places in Upwold are claiming a part in Walder's story and tying ribbons to ancient apple trees said to mark his grave.

r.Mitwold/Golden Downs: Just south of Hay, an old apple copse said to be Walder's grave is groaning with fruit, and it could host a folly, a sinecure shrine or an inspirational tomb if the resources are provided.

Home from the wars.d: Tens of thousands of humans and orcs died in the Greensward, souring the earth. Most survivors left, and only friars and ghosts remained in any numbers. Working from Honour's Rest, friars had begun using liao to lay ghosts to rest, but the Marcher Assembly acknowledged it needed help. Three mandates were proposed, each sending 50 doses of liao. The first would comfort the spirits, reducing the danger while the haunting slowly faded. The second would simply exorcise them, ending the haunting but leaving vicious remnants. Brother Oswin's third would aid Imperial dead and exorcise Jotun and thrall spirits, harming relations with the Mournwold thralls. Any of the mandates could be escalated to the General Assembly.

n.Jotun: The ghosts of Jotun warriors and thralls who died in the Greensward haunted the region alongside Imperial dead, and one proposed mandate would exorcise them rather than guide them across the Howling Abyss.
n.The Marches: Marcher friars at Honour's Rest struggled to lay the region's ghosts to rest, and the Marcher Assembly had to choose how priests would deal with them so that Marchers could return to farm the land.

t.Mournwold: The Marcher-held Mournwold faced a haunted region in the south that discouraged resettlement, and one option risked souring relations with the territory's thralls.

r.Mournwold/Greensward: The Greensward was haunted by countless angry dead who re-enacted their battles around the ruins on moonless nights, and depending on the mandate chosen the haunting could be eased gradually or removed outright, though dangerous remnants would remain.

Honey off a thorn.d: Since Wintermark gave Skarsind to the Imperial Orcs, many orcs arriving there want to farm and prosper rather than fight. Groups already accepted by the egregore, such as the Liberated and former Hierro, have struggled for acceptance. The options put forward were: 'War is in our Soul', limiting membership to committed soldiers; 'Building a Nation', welcoming any loyal orc; Irontide Lok's variant, which places the legions at the nation's heart; and Anka Fleshbinder's 'Life is Precious', which would open the nation to soldiers of any species. If no mandate passed, the status quo would continue. The civil service could not predict the full consequences of any of them.

n.Imperial Orcs: The Assembly was asked to define the nation's identity: a purely martial people, open heirs building a homeland, a legion-centred nation, or even one open to humans. The choice could drive away the Liberated and some Hierro, and could change how the nation elects its senators.
n.Jotun: Jotun thralls who met Imperial Orcs saw no affinity with them, but a 'Building a Nation' mandate might lead some to settle in Skarsind. The Jotun's acceptance of humans and orcs alike, as seen in the Mournwold, was cited in support of Anka's mandate.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the Liberated, who now struggle for acceptance among the orcs, were freed in Sarvos, and the Unbroken once hired a ship from Sarvos.
n.The Marches: Mentioned in passing: the fighting against the Jotun in the Mournwold is cited as evidence that not all enemies separate orcs and humans.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's senators began giving up Skarsind in 379YE in gratitude for the return of the Crown of Three Tears, and most orc slaves held in Wintermark chose exile after the rebellion.

t.Mournwold: Mentioned in passing: the Empire's experience fighting the Jotun here is cited to show that some enemies accept humans and orcs alike.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: the Liberated, former Jarmish slaves, were emancipated here, and the Unbroken sailed east from here on a hired vessel and were never seen again.
t.Skarsind: Orcs settling Skarsind, many with no interest in war, are at the heart of the dispute. The Foreman of the Mines of Gulhule refuses to let orc citizens work its mines, and the chosen mandate will shape who may make a home here.

Judged by their company.d: The Temple of the Seven Virtues in Nemoria, funded by the Senate and staffed by Imperial volunteers, drew local pilgrims, sightseers and some opposition. Ressia i Afanera i Guerra, the sutannir from Feroz who runs it, refused would-be priests he judged insincere, including sworn warriors of the Asavean God of War and slaves sent by their owners, several of whom offered money. The Synod could refuse all training, train a carefully chosen few, or open training widely, which was estimated to add 10 Thrones a season to the Virtue fund. The Synod upheld an inquisition of Almodin Oktístis. Zemress Islanders in Segura feared he would put idolatrous symbols into the Iron Qanat, which he would certainly do.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel ship merchants are listed among the foreign traders who come to Nemoria for luxuries and rare materials.
n.Highguard: Mentioned in passing: Highborn missionaries and wayfarers are among the Imperial volunteers serving as priests at the Nemoria temple.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn priests are central to the Nemoria temple: its overseer Ressia i Afanera i Guerra and the liaison Franco i Erigo are both Freeborn. At home, the Zemress Islanders in Segura objected to Almodin Oktístis decorating the Iron Qanat with Asavean idols, whatever the Coast's wider tolerance of the Asavean temple on its shores.
n.The League: League priests serve at the Nemoria temple, and one Asavean noble claimed a powerful League citizen would vouch for his slave. A Tassato printing house produced the popular pamphlet on the Asavean gods, and Oktístis had built a casino in Temeschwar.
n.Urizen: Mentioned in passing: the newly completed runeforge near Cargo is listed among the commissions Almodin Oktístis oversaw for the Senate.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Almodin Oktístis built a fortification in Varushka, and the page notes the recent controversy over its 'defilement'.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: Ressia i Afanera i Guerra, the sutannir who runs the Nemoria temple, comes from Feroz.
t.Redoubt: Mentioned in passing: the runeforge near Cargo, built under Almodin Oktístis, is listed among his Senate commissions.
t.Segura: Segura welcomed the Senate's commission of the Iron Qanat, but its Zemress refugee community demanded assurance that Almodin Oktístis would not build Asavean idols into it, saying they would rather go without the great work than accept idolatry.
t.Tassato: The Honourable Press in Tassato printed 'A Primer on the Asavean Gods', which spread along the Blood Red Roads, and refused to reveal who paid for it.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: a casino in Temeschwar is listed among the commissions Almodin Oktístis oversaw for the Senate.

r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The Iron Qanat, a fortified irrigation great work planned for the Sobral Grasses, could turn the sandy soil into rich farmland. The architect's insistence on working his gods' symbols into its foundations alarmed the Zemress settlers.
r.Tassato/Tassato Regario: The Honourable Press of Tassato Regario was the source of the widely copied Asavean religion pamphlet. It defended the work as helping the faithful resist Asavean priests and kept its patron secret.

Leaves and fruit.d: Johanna of Ravensfell designed the White Roads, linking Casfall to Bastion and Bastion to Necropolis and Reikos. They would cost 120 wains of white granite and 240 crowns, and would enrich those territories and the Virtue's Rest hostels. The Custodes Clavium, approached by Lev of the Unbound, offered to refurbish the Basilica for 15 wains of white granite and 5 of weirwood, paying the labour themselves, and to revive the Speaker title, with 10 liao and 20 Synod votes. Benefactors also proposed the Cinderpath Exchange, where white granite would be bought at a fair price. It would come with a Cinderpath Benefactor title and optional Assembly mandates, but would reduce Bourse supply. The Basilica work and the Speaker title were completed before Summer 383YE.

n.Dawn: Mentioned in passing: some virtuous Dawnish folk would heed a General Assembly mandate condemning market forces and bring white granite to the Cinderpath Exchange.
n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: a planned church carving shows the exemplar Zemress with her boot on the chest of a Grendel pirate.
n.Highguard: The Highborn were offered White Roads, a refurbished Basilica of the Seven Doors with a restored Speaker of the Highborn Assembly, and a fair-price white granite exchange. The Basilica and the Speaker title were completed before Summer 383YE.
n.Imperial Orcs: Mentioned in passing: some virtuous orcs would heed a General Assembly mandate against market greed and bring white granite to the Cinderpath Exchange.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: some virtuous Navarr would heed a General Assembly mandate promoting fair prices for white granite.
n.The Brass Coast: Mentioned in passing: the idea that market forces are unvirtuous was thought unlikely to gain traction there, though scholars mused about a Freeborn Assembly Speaker at Atalaya.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the League's Blood Red Roads were the benchmark for the White Roads, scholars imagined a League Assembly Speaker at Capodomus Cathedral, and the anti-market idea was expected to find little favour there.
n.Varushka: Mentioned in passing: Varushka was noted as producing better white granite than Highguard, and as unlikely to embrace the fair-price ideal.
n.Wintermark: Mentioned in passing: Wintermark's pilgrim roads in Kallavesa had left Highguard looking behind, and some virtuous Winterfolk might heed a General Assembly mandate on white granite.

t.Bastion: The White City was to be the hub of the proposed White Roads, and its Basilica of the Seven Doors was refurbished as the seat of the restored Speaker of the Highborn Assembly before Summer 383YE.
t.Casinea: Casinea's quarries produce white granite, the proposed White Roads would start from Casfall, and the Cinderpath Exchange was proposed for a village near its eastern borders.
t.Kallavesa: Mentioned in passing: the Senate's pilgrim roads and bridges commissioned in its marshes in Winter 379YE were cited as a contrast with roadless Highguard.
t.Karsk: Mentioned in passing: Karsk's existing road network was cited to show how far Highguard lagged behind.
t.Madruga: Mentioned in passing: scholars speculated about a Speaker for the Freeborn Assembly with offices at Atalaya.
t.Necropolis: A proposed White Road along the River Couros would link Bastion to Necropolis, helping pilgrims and enriching its businesses and farms.
t.Reikos: Reikos would gain a White Road to Tabernacle, possibly extended to High Chalcis and Casca's Doom, to aid its rebuilding and wealth. Its Vigilant Swan produces white granite but never enough to meet demand.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: scholars imagined a Speaker for the League Assembly based in Capodomus Cathedral.

r.Bastion/Stoneside: The proposed White Road from Casfall to the White City would run through Stoneside's light woods.
r.Casinea/Casfall: Casfall was to be the starting point of the proposed White Road, connecting the Blood Red Roads to Sybela and Bastion.
r.Casinea/Mareholm: Mareholm's mineral-rich hills, crossed by the trade routes to Anvil, were proposed as the home of the Cinderpath Exchange, a ministry buying white granite at a fair price.

Make good use.d: A Feni warband of roughly a thousand fighters, which the Spring Equinox efforts had failed to stop, was raiding across the Mournwold, chiefly from the Chalkdowns. Its concealing magic had apparently failed, letting scouts observe its camps. No conjunctions were found, but any Imperial army taking an offensive order in the Mournwold could destroy it by inflicting at least 400 casualties. Otherwise farms and businesses would lose 36 rings each season and herb gardens two herbs. The Alderly enclave could not be found without someone giving the Herald of the Council the means to locate it. In Hahnmark, raids centred on Southridge carried the same penalties, and two conjunctions were identified.

n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Alderly Feni enclave is said to have resisted the Jotun occupation of the Mournwold as well as the later Imperial liberation.
n.The Marches: Marcher farms, businesses and herb gardens in the Mournwold faced heavy losses unless an army dealt with the raiders. Suspicion also grew among other Marchers that the insular Alderly folk, rumoured to have Feni blood, had drifted from Marcher custom or were colluding with the Feni.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Hahnmark suffered renewed Feni ambushes on farms, businesses and herb gardens. Two conjunctions were identified that offered a chance to strike back at the raiders.

t.Hahnmark: Several Feni warbands, centred on Southridge, raided across Hahnmark. Unless they were stopped, every farm and business would lose 36 rings of production and each herb garden two herbs.
t.Mournwold: A Feni warband of around a thousand fighters raided across the territory, threatening a 36-ring loss to every farm and business and two herbs to each herb garden each season. Any Imperial army taking an offensive order there could destroy it.
t.Upwold: Mentioned in passing: the large Feni warband was sighted travelling across Upwold before raiding in northern Mournwold.

r.Hahnmark/Kalpamark: Feni raiding bands extended their reach from Southridge into prosperous Kalpamark.
r.Hahnmark/Southridge: Southridge, long suspected of hiding a Feni community in its hills and gullies, was the centre of the renewed Hahnmark raids.
r.Hahnmark/Valasmark: Feni bands were sighted raiding in militant Valasmark, west of their Southridge base.
r.Hahnmark/Wood Heath: Wood Heath was strangely given a wide berth by the Feni raiders, despite the limited defence its folk could muster.
r.Mournwold/Alderly: Alderly reported no Feni attacks at all, even though it shelters a hidden Feni enclave that no Imperial force has been able to find. This drew suspicion of collusion onto its insular charcoal burners and woodcutters.
r.Mournwold/Chalkdowns: The Chalkdowns were the main focus of the Feni warband, whose disguised camps scouts were able to approach and assess now that the Feni's concealing magic had failed.

Mean what you say.d: Autumn magic shielding Bay of Catazar traders from Grendel pirates was fading. Fleets from Tassato, Sarvos, the Brass Coast, Highguard and Urizen faced poorer trade returns. Wintermark, Dawnish and Navarr magicians raised defences in fens and Urizen mountains. Spiral's trods were restored, and the Colossus of Sarvos reshaped itself into Empress Giselle. The Reapers enchanted the Mournwold's farms. Stars stayed hidden over Semmerholm, the Barrens and Zenith, and veils covered several territories. In the Conclave, Adamant offered a stone academy and a Master of the Koboldi, Eleonaris offered a research boon, and Sadogua offered gifts. Agramant thanked four magicians, offered heart's blood and proposed a parley.

n.Dawn: The Dawnish witches of Summer Dawning Relentless, aided by House de Gauvain, raised a Frozen Citadel in Limus, while Dawn's own Semmerholm still lay under a starless Night shroud of magnitude fifty.
