n.Druj: The stars remained hidden over Druj-held Barrens and Zenith, and new magical fortifications in the fens and Urizen's mountains stood ready to resist any Druj advance.
n.Grendel: Grendel pirates in the Bay of Catazar had been confounded by Autumn magic, but the protection was fading and they might soon raid freely again. Agramant also boasted of catastrophic Grendel losses at the Black Plateau in Spiral.
n.Highguard: Highborn fleets faced poorer trade returns this season, and a scrying-blocking veil with heavy dark fog lay over Necropolis.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: named as a possible invader that the new fenland defences would have resisted, and Jotun-held Liathaven was among the places where the stars had been missing in 381YE.
n.Navarr: The Eternal Family raised a Frozen Citadel in Caeli, and the Voice of the Quiet Forest restored Spiral's trods. A Navarr Assembly mandate puzzled priests, and Arhallogen demanded a meeting with up to four Navarr vates.
n.The Brass Coast: Brass Coast fleets faced poorer trade returns this season, and a veil fell over Madruga once the nightly phantasmagoric displays ended.
n.The League: The Colossus of Sarvos now depicts Empress Giselle, and Dripping Echoes defences guarded the Morass. Tassato and Sarvos fleets faced poorer trade returns, Sarvos lay under a veil, and Sadogua was tending the ailing Richard of Holberg.
n.The Marches: The Reapers' Summer enchantment promised excellent Mournwold harvests, and the North Fens gained magical defences. A Marcher Assembly mandate confused priests, and Sadogua invited a Master Pearl to request a boon.
n.Thule: A Penumbral Veil was reported over Urdur in Otkodov, and it was unclear whether Nithoggir, Sküld or Verthandi were similarly shrouded.
n.Urizen: Frozen Citadels were raised in Limus and Caeli to guard against the Druj. Urizeni fleets faced poorer trade returns, and a veil with dark fog covered Redoubt.
n.Wintermark: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised the Dripping Echoes of the Fen over Kallavesa's West Marsh, the Morass and the North Fens, shielding these wetlands against Jotun or Druj invasion.

t.Bay of Catazar: Autumn magic had slowed time around Imperial ships to help them escape Grendel pirates, but captains feared it would dissipate entirely by the end of the Solstice.
t.Bregasland: Its North Fens were protected by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen raised by the Sussivari Frost Coven, though the defences were not tested.
t.Holberg: The Morass was fortified with the Dripping Echoes of the Fen by Wintermark magicians, ready to resist any hostile force.
t.Kallavesa: West Marsh gained the Dripping Echoes of the Fen from the Sussivari Frost Coven, which would have met any invasion with stiff resistance.
t.Liathaven: Mentioned in passing: noted as one of the places where the stars were absent for most of 381YE.
t.Madruga: A scrying-blocking veil with heavy dark fog lay over Madruga after the nightly phantasmagoric displays, and its fleets faced poorer trade returns.
t.Morrow: A Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae was raised in Caeli by the Navarr Eternal Family, ready to repel any Druj attack.
t.Mournwold: The Reapers' Strong Oxen, Golden Sunshine enchantment strengthened beasts and workers and bolstered crops, promising excellent harvests for Marcher and thrall alike. Agramant also offered a boon to whoever laid curses on the territory.
t.Necropolis: A ritual shroud warped the stars over Necropolis, blocking scrying and bringing heavy, dark fog.
t.Otkodov: Merchants reported a Penumbral Veil over Urdur, but whether its other regions were shrouded remained unclear without scrying.
t.Redoubt: A Frozen Citadel was raised in Limus, and a veil with inky clouds and dark fog hindered scrying over the territory.
t.Sarvos: The Colossus reshaped itself from the First Butcher into Empress Giselle, to many citizens' approval. A veil also hung over the territory, and its fleets faced poorer trade returns.
t.Semmerholm: The stars stayed missing beneath a Night shroud of magnitude fifty that blocked lesser scrying, and naga who spent time there felt a strong urge to secrecy.
t.Spiral: The Voice of the Quiet Forest restored its trods along new paths that skirt but never cross the Black Plateau, binding Spiral back into the trod network.
t.Tassato: Fleets from Tassato faced poorer returns from trade during the coming season.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Empress Giselle's tomb there was described by many as gaudy and not really a monument to her.
t.The Barrens: The stars remained absent above the Barrens, impeding scrying and heightening naga secretiveness, with the shroud expected to last until shortly before Winter 382YE.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether the Penumbral Veil over Urdur also covered Verthandi.
t.Zenith: The stars vanished from Zenith's sky shortly before the Spring Equinox, impeding scrying and affecting naga who spent time there.

r.Bregasland/North Fens: The Sussivari Frost Coven raised the Dripping Echoes of the Fen here, ready to resist any invader.
r.Holberg/The Morass: The Morass was protected by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen raised by Wintermark magicians.
r.Kallavesa/West Marsh: West Marsh's wetlands were guarded by the Dripping Echoes of the Fen from the Sussivari Frost Coven.
r.Morrow/Caeli: The Navarr Eternal Family raised a Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae in Caeli's mountains.
r.Otkodov/Nithoggir: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether Nithoggir also lay under the Penumbral Veil.
r.Otkodov/Sküld: Mentioned in passing: it was unclear whether Sküld also lay under the Penumbral Veil.
r.Otkodov/Urdur: Merchants and pedlars reported that the ritual Drawing the Penumbral Veil had been worked over Urdur.
r.Redoubt/Limus: Summer Dawning Relentless, aided by House de Gauvain, raised a Frozen Citadel of Cathan Canae in Limus.

More work.d: Statements of principle passed by the Assembly of the Nine with a greater majority now carry as much weight as national assembly statements, but with wider reach. Several further changes were proposed but not enacted. Vibia of Fossegrimm Spire suggested escalating virtue assembly statements to the Nine. The Senate could restore cardinals as voting senators, which would abolish the Conscience of the Senate. Abigail of Forestgard proposed eight cardinal palaces in Bastion. Bishop Jago and Teodora Bezavina suggested ending protection from repeated revocation, or barring revoked citizens from the same title for a year. Bonewall Col's statement on virtuous ancestors produced no clear effect.

n.Highguard: The Highborn Abigail of Forestgard proposed eight cathedral-palaces for the cardinals ringing Bastion, which would cement the White City as the global heart of the Way if the Senate commissioned them.
n.Imperial Orcs: Bonewall Col's statement on recognising virtuous ancestors met a mixed and uneasy response among orc congregations. Many feared it would create an orc-only category of inspiration, but Severin's sermon stopped it from causing wider conflict or a clear effect.
n.The League: League figures led the debate. Severin von Holberg's encyclical started it, Bishop Orlando di Holberg argued that the national assemblies had grown at the Synod's expense, and Bishop Jago di Temeschwar proposed strengthening revocation, which a League prince privately criticised.
n.Urizen: Vibia of Fossegrimm Spire proposed that the Senate escalate virtue assembly statements to the Assembly of the Nine. Architects from the School of Epistemology helped draw up plans for the proposed cardinal palaces.
n.Varushka: The constitutional scholar Teodora Bezavina of Delev worked with Bishop Jago on the revocation proposals. She persuaded him to soften a permanent ban on reappointment to a one-year ban.

t.Bastion: Bastion was proposed as the site of eight cardinal palaces ringed around the White City with parks and monuments. The commission would cost 120 white granite, 40 weirwood and 320 crowns and take six months to build.
t.Casinea: The palace proposal came from Abigail of Forestgard, a dedicate of Pride from an old chapter in Casinea who had studied the Houses of Virtue in Timoj.
t.Holberg: Holberg is home to Severin von Holberg, whose encyclical prompted the debate, and to Bishop Orlando di Holberg of the University of Holberg. Holberg engineers also helped plan the proposed palaces.
t.Karov: Karov is home to Teodora Bezavina of Delev, the constitutional scholar who co-authored the proposals to strengthen the Synod's power of revocation.
t.Morrow: Vibia of Fossegrimm Spire in Morrow proposed the compromise of escalating greater-majority virtue assembly statements to the Assembly of the Nine, which the Constitutional Court judged constitutional in principle.
t.Skarsind: Bonewall Col's statement on virtuous ancestors was distributed among Skarsind's congregations. It drew a mixed and largely disapproving response and created no clear effect.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: Tassato is not named on the page; its only apparent link is the opening vignette of a League prince walking a riverbank and criticising Bishop Jago.
t.Temeschwar: Bishop Jago Heshel di Temeschwar of the Church of the Golden Orator proposed ending the protection from repeated revocation, or barring revoked citizens from their title for a year.

r.Casinea/Woodwych: Forestgard, an old chapter in Woodwych, is home to Abigail, who proposed building palaces for the cardinals in Bastion.

Ratify Thule peace treaty.d: The ratified treaty grants five years of peace in exchange for the Empire ceding Crow's Ridge in Skarsind to the Thule. The Thule agree to free enslaved Imperial citizens and their descendants for a mutually agreed ransom. They will cast Rivers of Life on Sermersuaq if the Empire supplies the mana, will make no alliance with the Druj, and will share strategic information about them. Neither side will raid or send soldiers into the other's territory without agreement, though the Thule clarified they may still move troops in Silver Peaks, Krevsaty and Crow's Ridge. The clause on attacks is not a mutual defence pact. The Thule are treated as foreigners, and the Constitutional Court still required a copy of the text.

n.Druj: The Thule pledged to make no alliance with the Druj, said they wished to see them destroyed, and agreed to pass strategic information about them to the Empire.
n.Imperial Orcs: The Imperial Orcs lose Crow's Ridge in Skarsind to the Thule under the treaty, though the Thule declared them welcome to visit the region.
n.Thule: The Thule of Otkodov gain Crow's Ridge and five years of peace with the Empire, in return for freeing Imperial slaves for ransom, forgoing raids and any Druj alliance, and being treated as foreigners.
n.Varushka: Varushka gains peace with the Thule, although the Thule reserve the right to keep moving soldiers through Krevsaty in Karsk.
n.Wintermark: Wintermark's Sermersuaq may receive the Thule's Rivers of Life ritual if the Empire provides the mana, while the Thule keep the right to send soldiers into the Silver Peaks.

t.Karsk: Karsk is covered by the peace, but the Thule clarified they remain free to send soldiers into Krevsaty, the region of Karsk they hold.
t.Otkodov: Otkodov is the Thule homeland with which the treaty was made, through the Imperial Ambassador to Otkodov.
t.Sermersuaq: The Thule agreed to cast Rivers of Life on Sermersuaq in the coming season, provided the Empire offered the required mana.
t.Skarsind: The Empire ceded the Skarsind region of Crow's Ridge to the Thule as the price of the five-year peace.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: The Thule explicitly retained the freedom to send their soldiers into Krevsaty despite the treaty's ban on troops entering the other side's territory.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule clarified that they may continue to send soldiers into the Silver Peaks under the treaty.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: Crow's Ridge was formally ceded by the Empire to the Thule, who said Imperial Orcs would be welcome to visit it.

Set in stone.d: Morale in the Mourn had been rising with the fortification of Freemoor and Greensward, Sarcombe's charter and the Singing Caves becoming a Marcher national resource. Then the Conclave backed the casting of Rivers Run Red, and the anger soon turned to weary resignation. The Mourners resolved to protect themselves. Richard of Holberg offered four options. Menhirs in the Mourn would give mana and halve curse casualties there. Protection for the Marches would halve curse effects nationwide. Menhirs in the Marches would quarter them and add mana. A Wonder of the Known World would add mana, farm wealth, a fifth-strength curse effect and an improved Imperial Breadbasket. The last three depended on Richard being alive, and he has since died.

n.Jotun: The Mourners accepted that the curse had shortened the Jotun war there, and expected the Jotun to return one day. That fear is why they want defences against the Military Council ever cursing their land again.
n.Navarr: The Navarr cast Rivers Run Red on Therunin with the Conclave's leave. Navarr travellers who tried to justify the need for it in the Mourn only fuelled the anger there.
n.The League: Mentioned in passing: the menhir designs come from the League architect Richard of Holberg.
n.The Marches: The Marchers were offered menhir networks paid from the Singing Caves' stockpile of over 100 wains of mithril. These ranged from protecting the Mourn alone to a nationwide wonder giving mana, farm wealth and strong protection against curses on any Marcher territory.

t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Holberg appears only in the name of the architect Richard of Holberg.
t.Mournwold: The Mourn's people felt betrayed by the Conclave's backing of Rivers Run Red. Their landskeepers proposed menhirs that would give each farm mana and halve curse casualties there, which would lay to rest their last doubt about their place in the Empire.
t.Therunin: Rivers Run Red was cast on Therunin, and that casting reopened old wounds in the Mournwold.

r.Mournwold/Freemoor: Mentioned in passing: work to fortify Freemoor was among the news that lifted spirits in the Mourn.
r.Mournwold/Greensward: Mentioned in passing: work to fortify Greensward was among the news that lifted spirits in the Mourn.

Stings like the truth.d: The Whisper Gallery now works through mortal agents. Leontes the Scribe was stabbed in his garden, and Peter of Hintown's husband Dorcas was poisoned with Virus Lunarae, apparently by Antonia di Sarvos, who remains at large. The Senate could empower the Conclave or magistrates, and the Synod could direct the Silent Bell against such agents. Hannah's Silence, a secretive Highborn chapter led by Exarch Zipporah, proposed replacing Livia, having the Highborn assembly elect the Seer, or restricting publication of past-life visions. Livia's publishers, Spider's Vantage Spire, instead offered wider distribution. The Senate funded distribution of Echoes of the Labyrinth to foreign trading nations. Sung's herald Curious Breeze said it would probably attend Anvil.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: Grendel is not named; its only link is through the Spiral territory, which the page does not discuss directly.
n.Highguard: Hannah's Silence, a Highborn chapter, sent a delegation to Anvil to lobby Highborn senators to curb the Seer of the Gateway, including a controversial proposal that the Highborn National Assembly elect the Seer. Highborn benefactors were also noted as supporters of the Heirs of Lepidus.
n.The League: A League mountebank, Antonia di Sarvos, was believed by the militia to be the poisoner who targeted Peter of Hintown on the Whisper Gallery's instructions, and remains at large.
n.Urizen: Livia Cascade of Urizen faced calls for her replacement as Seer of the Gateway, while her Urizen publishers, the Spider's Vantage Spire, offered to spread her work further. The Senate then funded distribution of Echoes of the Labyrinth to foreign trading nations.

t.Necropolis: Hannah's Silence is based in the Necropolis, where Exarch Zipporah preached publicly against the Seer of the Gateway's publications before sending a delegation to Anvil.
t.Reikos: Mentioned in passing: the fall of Reikos left many Highborn chapterless, some of whom are said to have joined Hannah's Silence.
t.Sarvos: Militia investigating the attempted poisoning searched Sarvos and found that the suspect, Antonia di Sarvos, had vanished from their usual haunts.
t.Spiral: Mentioned in passing: the territory is not directly referenced; the word appears only in the title of the eternal Sung, the Spiral Dancer.
t.Temeschwar: Mentioned in passing: Peter of Hintown's bodyguard Alva, a Temeschwari woman, recognised the poison symptoms in time to help save Dorcas.

Talk softly.d: The Great Forest Orcs stored Rivers of Life after realising its danger near the vallorn. Recovered with Navarr and Highborn aid, they no longer need herb support, though the Holt of the Oak has stalled. Around a hundred asked to join stridings for a year, but only with a Senate motion or a strongly passed Navarr Assembly statement; this risked them mapping the Empire and their briar allies coming too. The Thule sent Rak to Anvil for a last attempt at a treaty, warned over magic in the Silver Peaks, massed armies in Sermersuaq and Karsk, and freed Wintermark slaves paid for by Eska Crowspeaker. Jotun thralls awaited a Synod resolution. The Grendel rejected peace but ceded Spiral.

n.Druj: Mentioned in passing: there was no news of the Druj, though the Great Forest Orcs hoped to return to the Barrens once the Druj were defeated.
n.Grendel: The Salt Lords flatly refused the offered peace treaty, embassy and mithril trade, called Solen's Doubt a setback rather than a defeat, and formally ceded Spiral to the Empire while the Black Plateau endured.
n.Highguard: The Highborn were thanked for helping the Great Forest Orcs recover, and visiting orcs were greatly impressed by the gardens of High Chalcis in Reikos.
n.Imperial Orcs: The stream of Thule orc merchants coming through Crow's Ridge into Skarsind slowed to a trickle. The Thule also offered to negotiate a mithril route through the Silver Peaks into Skarsind.
n.Jotun: The Jotun were expected to possibly conquer southern Sermersuaq, prompting Thule offers over the Pride of Ikka's Tears mine. Separately, the former Jotun thralls awaited a Synod resolution of their concerns with the Way.
n.Navarr: The Navarr were asked, by Senate motion or Assembly statement, to let around a hundred Great Forest Orcs travel with their stridings for a year, and the orcs thanked them for their aid. Merel was advised to ready a coven for the Dance of Navarr and Thorn at the Thule parley.
n.The League: A Grendel envoy came under a flag of truce to the docks of Sarvos to reject Consul Aureliana di Sarvos's peace offer before a jeering crowd.
n.The Marches: Continued improvement in the Mournwold depended on a satisfactory outcome for the Jotun thralls, whose representative Sigdór had left the matter with the Synod.
n.Thule: The Thule sent Rak to Anvil for a final attempt at a treaty before the 379YE peace expired, warned against harmful magic in the Silver Peaks, and moved additional armies into Sermersuaq and Karsk.
n.Urizen: The Grendel ceded Spiral to the Empire and mockingly wished the Urizen luck reclaiming the poisoned wasteland while the Black Plateau persisted.
n.Varushka: Thule merchant traffic through the mountains into Varushka dwindled. The Thule massed armies in Krevsaty in Karsk and again raised an icy magical fortress there.
n.Wintermark: About two dozen former Wintermark slaves, freed by Eska Crowspeaker's payment, reached Fjellreven Hall and resolved to join her congregation to repay their debt.

t.Bay of Catazar: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel noted that they hold other territories on the Bay of Catazar, and further information on their threat to fleets there was referenced.
t.Karsk: The Thule moved additional armies into Krevsaty and raised a glittering magical fortress of ice and iron spikes, possibly in preparation for war.
t.Miekarova: Mentioned in passing: Rak issued his statement on Sermersuaq from the Thule embassy in Miekarova.
t.Mournwold: The territory's improving situation rested on finding a satisfactory resolution to the Jotun thralls' problems with the Way.
t.Otkodov: Mentioned in passing: any Thule claim on the bounty of the Silver Peaks mithril mine would be a matter for the Ambassador to Otkodov, Yevgeni Katzev.
t.Reikos: Great Forest Orcs visited High Chalcis, whose gardens would begin benefiting Reikos herb gardens after the Summer solstice. Reikos's assistance had helped the orcs recover.
t.Sarvos: A lone Grendel envoy landed at the Sarvos docks under a flag of truce to reject the Empire's peace offer and cede Spiral, departing amid heckling.
t.Sermersuaq: The Thule warned against magic harming their people in the Silver Peaks, massed troops there and offered deals over the mithril mine. Freed Wintermark slaves arrived in the East Floes.
t.Skarsind: Thule merchant traffic into Skarsind slowed to a trickle, and the Thule offered to negotiate a mithril route from the Silver Peaks into the territory.
t.Spiral: The Grendel formally ceded all control of Spiral to the Empire while the Black Plateau persists, leaving maddened remnants of their armies around Apstrus.
t.The Barrens: Mentioned in passing: the Great Forest Orcs kept the Rivers of Life text for their hoped-for return to the Barrens after the Druj are defeated.
t.Therunin: The Great Forest Orcs became a common sight trading with the Navarr, herb and business penalties ended after the Summer solstice, and around a hundred orcs sought to join stridings from Therunin.
t.Verthandi: Mentioned in passing: the freed Wintermark slaves had worked a farm near Samkǒma in Hengill supplying the settlement with a hardy root.

r.Karsk/Krevsaty: Imperial scouts reported additional Thule armies and a newly raised magical fortress of ice and iron spikes in the hills here.
r.Sermersuaq/East Floes: A caravan of freed Wintermark slaves was escorted by Thule warriors to within sight of Fjellreven Hall in the East Floes.
r.Sermersuaq/Silver Peaks: The Thule moved more armies onto the slopes, warned against harmful magic, and offered either a mithril route or to seize the Pride of Ikka's Tears mine.
r.Skarsind/Crow’s Ridge: The once steady flow of Thule orc merchants through Crow's Ridge slowed to a trickle as the treaty's end approached.
r.Spiral/Apstrus: The Grendel said the insane remnants of their armies remained camped around Apstrus, leaving the Empire to deal with them.
r.Therunin/Lower Tarn Valley: The Great Forest Orcs continued building their new lives here, with weirwood-fed herb gardens and some farms tending goats and cows, though the Holt of the Oak stalled.
r.Therunin/Peakedge Song: Great Forest Orc apothecaries took temporary residence at Peakedge Stead as healers, and orc hunters encountered the trods in the Song.
r.Verthandi/Hengill: Mentioned in passing: the freed slaves had farmed near Samkǒma in Hengill under the Thule.

The same bed.d: From the Spring Equinox, nightly light shows over Madruga depicted Imperial victories, lifting Freeborn morale before fading near the Solstice. An earthquake centred on Ghita's Veils in the Sobral Grasses broke its ancient pillars and trenches, revealing they had contained mana; the site gained two ranks, though magicians suffered a shared nightmare. Cheaper upgrades for Ghita's Veils and the Garden of Sighs, and a proposed standing-stone great work across Segura, were offered for the Summer Solstice only. Prompted by the League Assembly, Menno van Ritsjhof proposed twin harbour towers guarding Siroc and the Lyceum, requiring a Senate commission. A Freeborn statement that military donations are not unprosperous drew little interest.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Grendel burning of Atalaya still stings the Freeborn, and the Drakes are said to be still fighting the remaining Grendel on the islands.
n.Jotun: Mentioned in passing: the Jotun are back in Kahraman, though the Freeborn are confident they can be beaten again.
n.Navarr: Mentioned in passing: some see similarities between the design of Ghita's Veils and patterns favoured by the Navarr.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn morale was lifted by the skyborne displays, Segura gained stronger mana flows and time-limited upgrade opportunities, Siroc was offered an ambitious sea defence, and the Freeborn largely shrugged off their assembly's statement on charity, insisting giving is a private matter.
n.The League: A League Assembly statement urged Menno van Ritsjhof, architect of Holberg's walls, to design fortifications for Madruga, and visitors from Sarvos and Tassato travelled to enjoy the lights.

t.Feroz: Mentioned in passing: people from Feroz travelled to Madruga to see the lights in the sky.
t.Holberg: Mentioned in passing: Menno van Ritsjhof is famed for his work on the walls of Holberg.
t.Kahraman: Mentioned in passing: the territory's renewed Jotun invasion worries the Freeborn, and people from Kahraman came to see the lights over Madruga.
t.Madruga: Nightly light shows of Imperial victories drew crowds to Madruga until shortly before the Solstice, and a proposed twin-tower fortification costing 100 wains of white granite, 20 of weirwood and 30 Thrones would guard Siroc and the Lyceum if the Senate commissions it.
t.Sarvos: Mentioned in passing: visitors from Sarvos came to see the lights, and Menno's unbuilt 'chain against chains' design for the city is recalled.
t.Segura: An earthquake strengthened mana flows across Segura, and a hakima proposed a standing-stone great work, needing a Senate motion or Wayleave, to yield 37 crystal mana across its mana sites, though another warned of astronomantic side effects.
t.Tassato: Mentioned in passing: visitors from Tassato travelled to Madruga to enjoy the lights in the sky.

r.Segura/Anduzjasse: Freer mana flows offered the owner of the Garden of Sighs a chance to upgrade it to rank three for a single wain of mithril, available only after the Summer Solstice.
r.Segura/Sobral Grasses: The quake shook the whole region, collapsed an old house in Anozel and wrecked Ghita's Veils, which gained two ranks as released mana surged and could be raised to rank six for four wains of mithril, while local magicians shared an ominous nightmare.

Weak and idle theme.d: The Freeborn Assembly unanimously assured the Islanders that they faced no enslavement and claimed the rebels had refused refuge, a claim the Islanders doubted. The Pride Assembly unanimously condemned allowing slaves to be taken on Imperial soil, and its words resonated far more. Seguran Freeborn spoke of their people's role in banning slavery twice, including Emperor Ahraz's emancipation of orcs, perhaps foreshadowed in a past-life vision. With the Suranni already dragged back in chains, the Islanders proposed a mandate urging every Freeborn to aid enslaved people. If passed, the Freeborn would act at once to protect any slaves crossing the border. A wider version could reach every nation.

n.Grendel: Mentioned in passing: the Zemress Islanders fled the threat of Grendel enslavement, and the story recalls a Freeborn shipwright drowned when the Grendel burnt the shipyards.
n.The Brass Coast: Freeborn across the Coast began questioning their national assembly's stance and taking pride in their history of abolition. A proposed mandate would have them rise at once to protect any slaves crossing the border.

t.Feroz: The Iron Confederacy was allowed to bring armies into Feroz and enslave the Suranni rebels sheltering there in full view, and this sparked the controversy.
t.Kalino: Mentioned in passing: the Duke of Kalino and his forces are named as those who attacked the slaves' camp.
t.Segura: The Zemress Islanders settled in Segura carried their abolitionist concerns to their Seguran neighbours, some of whom shared them and helped shape the proposed mandate.
